capability.howSuccessIsMeasured: Hidden tests read the application's end state, its audit log and the action ledger: the target record holds exactly the required values, no other record differs from the frozen baseline, every changed record has an accepted audited commit, every audited request traces to a real browser action in the ledger, the confirmation step was taken, and the refused input was corrected to the accepted form.
capability.name: Browser task in a real application
capability.whatIsTested: A task inside a real web application, driven through a real headless browser. The application runs inside the model's own network-none box from a frozen state; the model sees the page as a text snapshot with stable element references and acts through declared browser actions (open, snapshot, click, fill, select, press, back). The application's state, its own audit log of every mutating request and the engine's action ledger all sit outside the model's writable paths.
capability.whyItIsDifficult: The failure modes this exposes are acting on the wrong record (a decoy one digit away from the target), stopping before the confirmation step, leaving collateral changes on other records, and giving up when the application refuses an input. A correct-looking end state is not enough: the grader also requires that every change was driven through the application, so a state file written directly fails.
